subject: Clarify: data ephemerality assurance & model-training exclusion process
messages:
From: Sarah Holmes <sarah.holmes@finbook.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Nov 2028 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Qs about training & deletion timeline

Hi Connor / Grace,

Quick one from the security review: we need explicit language for our counsel and SREs. Two parts: 1) you state in the contract that Redwood does not use customer data to train general models — can you confirm that applies to all hosted APIs (including streaming) and to Dedicated capacity unless the customer opts in to fine-tuning? 2) retention: can you walk us through what is ephemeral vs persistent (caches, KV store, logs, snapshots) and the guaranteed deletion timeline once we call the deletion API or terminate the account?

Attached is the worksheet our GC filled out (FinBook_Security_Questions.xlsx) — we highlighted fields that need short, authoritative answers. Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow PST? We may need a brief statement our legal team can incorporate.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Holmes
Head of IT Security | FinBook
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Holmes <sarah.holmes@finbook.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Nov 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Qs about training & deletion timeline

Hi Sarah — thanks for the concise list. Short answers up front, then a quick breakdown so your counsel has language to use:

- Training: Redwood does not use customer content submitted via the API for training our public or internal foundation models by default. That covers hosted API requests (including streaming) and Dedicated instances. The one exception is explicit, documented opt-in for customers who contract for collaborative fine-tuning or managed tuning services — that is a separate agreement with clear data use terms.

- Deletion/ephemerality: We distinguish three categories:
  * Transient request data (in-flight buffers and per-request KV cache): retained only for the duration of the request and removed from hot memory; no durable storage is written.
  * Operational telemetry & short-term logs (request metadata, aggregated metrics): retained for billing, troubleshooting, and SLO observability. Default retention is 30 days for request-level logs; aggregated metrics are stored longer for product analytics (configurable).
  * Snapshots/backups and long-lived artifacts (model snapshots, customer-managed datasets on Dedicated): these are durable, and deletion from persistent store follows a multi-step process and confirmation window (typically 7–90 days depending on region and backup class).

I'll paste suggested contract language below and follow up with a diagram (redwood-ephemerality-diagram.png) and a filled worksheet answers set. If you want, Grace can provide the formal security attestation your legal team can drop into the contract.

Suggested language for counsel (editable):
"Redwood Inference represents and warrants that, except where Customer and Redwood have executed a separate written agreement expressly permitting use of Customer Data for model training or tuning, Redwood will not use Customer Data submitted to Redwood's inference endpoints to train or improve Redwood's general-purpose models. Transient in-memory artifacts used to serve requests are not persisted to durable model training datasets. Operational logs needed for billing and incident analysis are retained for a limited period (by default 30 days) and are deleted in accordance with Redwood's Data Retention Policy. Durable backups and snapshots are deleted following the customer's deletion request per the Data Deletion Process, which may include a short retention window to allow for forensic review and recovery (default 7 days for operational backups, up to 90 days for archival snapshots in certain regions)."

Next steps: I'll attach the completed worksheet and a short process note on how to trigger account deletion (API + portal steps). If you want a one-paragraph executive attestation signed by Grace, say the word and we'll route to legal.

-Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Holmes <sarah.holmes@finbook.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Nov 2028 20:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Qs about training & deletion timeline

Thanks Connor — that helps. Couple of clarifying follow-ups from our infra team: 1) when you say "not persisted to durable model training datasets," does that also include temporary disk-backed spill files used during large responses (for example, when using KV cache or long context windows)? 2) what about backups/snapshots created for debugging of customer-specific Dedicated instances — do those follow the same deletion timeline or are they treated differently?

If you can confirm the path for the disk-backed spill and Dedicated-instance snapshots, we should be able to close this loop and I can share the language with GC.

-Sarah
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Holmes <sarah.holmes@finbook.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Qs about training & deletion timeline

Hi Sarah — Grace from Security & Compliance here. Quick confirmations and final text you can hand to GC.

1) Disk-backed spill files / swap / temporary local SSD:
- For hosted API: ephemeral spill files that may be written to local ephemeral storage during a request are encrypted at rest for the lifecycle of the request and are removed immediately after the request completes. These artifacts are not copied to durable object stores or training datasets. We treat them as "request ephemeral" and do not surface them to any training pipelines.
- For Dedicated: customers can opt for local-only volumes; for debugging we may create a support snapshot with customer consent. Those snapshots are labeled with the customer's account id and are stored in a restricted backup partition. They are deleted on request; standard deletion flow for such support snapshots is 7 days, but customers can request immediate destruction and an attestation if needed (we'll route HSM-backed key destruction and provide an audit log).

2) Backups & snapshots:
- Support/debug snapshots (created with explicit customer consent or as part of a support engagement) follow the support snapshot retention policy (default 7 days).
- Scheduled backups/archival snapshots (e.g., for Dedicated archival, region compliance) may have longer retention depending on the storage tier — we disclose these in the deployment manifest and they follow region-specific retention windows (configurable up to 90 days).

3) Deletion workflow (high-level):
- API/Portal request: Customer issues Delete Account or Delete Data via console or Data Deletion API.
- Pre-check: automated validation for outstanding compliance holds, billing reconciliation.
- Quarantine window: short default period (7 days) for forensic review and recovery; configurable and can be set to 0 for immediate deletion with attestation.
- Final purge: on completion, data is removed from live stores, snapshots retired, and relevant encryption keys rotated/destroyed where key material is customer-scoped. Audit entries are generated and can be exported.

Formal attestation paragraph (copy/paste for contract):
"Redwood Inference confirms that Customer Data submitted to Redwood's inference endpoints will not be used to train, tune, or otherwise improve Redwood's shared model assets unless such use is explicitly governed by a separate written agreement and opt-in by the Customer. Transient disk-backed spill files and in-memory caches used to serve requests are ephemeral and are not persisted into training repositories. Support or debug snapshots of Dedicated deployments are created only with customer consent and are managed under a documented retention and deletion workflow; standard support snapshots are retained for up to seven (7) days unless otherwise configured. Customers may request immediate destruction and an audit attestation for any retained artifacts."

If FinBook would like a custom retention profile (shorter telemetry retention, immediate snapshot purge, or a zero-quarantine deletion flow), we can document that in the Dedicated deployment manifest and include it in the Order Form. Happy to set up a 30-minute call if you want the security engineering team present.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: completed worksheet (FinBook_Security_Questions.xlsx) and a small diagram describing the ephemeral vs durable boundary (redwood-ephemerality-diagram.png).
